description: **Presence is now declared, never inferred.** Every flag and every positional argument must declare exactly one of `presence="required"`, `presence="optional"` or `default=<value>`; declaring none or two is a registration-time error. `default=None` is refused with a redirect to `presence="optional"`, the arg `required=` field is deleted, a repeatable or dict flag no longer defaults silently to `[]` / `{}`, and a mutex member declares its own optionality instead of receiving an exemption.

**`ctx.provided(name)`, and presence published everywhere it is asked about.** `ctx.provided` answers whether the invocation caused a flag's value -- true for `cli`, `env`, `config` and `implied`, false for `default` and `infra` -- so no handler reconstructs that boolean out of `ctx.source`. `--dump-schema` emits a `presence` key on every flag and arg entry, plus a `default` exactly when presence is `"default"` (empty collections included); help renders exactly one marker per line (`[required]`, `[optional]` or `[default: <value>]`), with required positionals and declared empty collections now visible; and MCP tool schemas read requiredness straight off the declaration.

**A positional argument's bool default renders lowercase in help.** A positional now shows `[default: true]` / `[default: false]` exactly as a flag does; it rendered `[default: True]` through Python's own `str`, so a single help page could show both spellings of the same value. Every other value type -- strings, numbers, collections -- already rendered identically on both surfaces and is now pinned that way.
